def Def2 (σ : ArithmeticSentence) : Prop := ℕ↓[ℒₒᵣ] ⊧ σ

def Def3 (K : Def1) : Prop := ∀ σ ∈ K, Def2 σ

def Def4 (K : Def1) : Prop := Entailment.Consistent (K : ArithmeticTheory)

def Def11 (K : Def1) : Prop := Theory.theory (K : ArithmeticTheory) ⊆ K
a_raw: {"translation":"For any arithmetic sentence σ, Def2(σ) means that σ is true in the standard model of the natural numbers. For any set K of arithmetic sentences, Def3(K) means that for every arithmetic sentence σ, if σ belongs to K, then σ is true in the standard model; it does not require every true sentence to belong to K. Def4(K) means that K, used as an axiom set, does not prove a contradiction. Def11(K) means that for every arithmetic sentence σ, if σ is derivable from K as axioms, then σ belongs to K. The stated inclusion is from the set of theorems of K into K. These are separate definitions: Def4 does not assume Def3, and Def11 does not assume truth of the members of K or consistency of K."}
translation: For any arithmetic sentence σ, Def2(σ) means that σ is true in the standard model of the natural numbers. For any set K of arithmetic sentences, Def3(K) means that for every arithmetic sentence σ, if σ belongs to K, then σ is true in the standard model; it does not require every true sentence to belong to K. Def4(K) means that K, used as an axiom set, does not prove a contradiction. Def11(K) means that for every arithmetic sentence σ, if σ is derivable from K as axioms, then σ belongs to K. The stated inclusion is from the set of theorems of K into K. These are separate definitions: Def4 does not assume Def3, and Def11 does not assume truth of the members of K or consistency of K.

divergences.description: The excerpts give the intended readings of K and T but do not explicitly formulate soundness or deductive closure for K. Def3 and Def11 add names for these conditions without asserting that the intended K satisfies either one.

judgement.summary: Taking T to be the set of arithmetic sentences true in the standard natural numbers, Def2 defines membership in T and Def3 says exactly K ⊆ T. Def4 expresses ordinary proof-theoretic consistency, and Def11 requires every sentence derivable from K to belong to K, the correct direction for closure.
